title: Parish Notice: High Water
speaker: Saltmere Parish Council
text:
POSTED 11 DAYS AGO.
The pumps at the sluice are off until the county sends a part. Expect water to the first step on Quay Row and the whole of Chapel Lane.
Do not wade. Two people have gone in this month and one did not come out.
If you cannot get to the ferry, stay upstairs, keep a light in the window, and we will come door to door.
We did not come door to door. There was nobody left to send. - R. Teague, warden (added by hand)

title: Scrawl on the Market Tiles
text:
Written in gutting-table chalk, three feet high, across the white tiles:
DON'T DRINK THE WATER
DON'T BOIL IT EITHER
IT CAME UP THE DRAINS FROM UNDER US
Below it, smaller, in a different hand: Nan drank it and she's fine. She's 80. She's fine.
Below that, in the first hand again: she is not fine.

title: Calder's Pages, 1 of 5
speaker: Dr. Ines Calder
text:
Taped under the auctioneer's desk, market hall.
I am splitting this up. If one place burns or floods, the rest keeps.
Start here, because this is where I understood it. I bought a crab off a man on this floor who could not lift his own box. Eight months later I read his file. He was the first one we put it in, and he lifted a steel door off its runners.
Elias calls that a result. I called it a man who used to sell me crab.
The other pages are where I pray and where I sleep.

title: Cold Store Receipt Book
speaker: Saltmere Fish Market
text:
Carbon copy, third sheet from the back.
ACCOUNT: VIGOR BIOTECH (SITE SERVICES), 14 months standing.
ITEM: Cold store bay 3, exclusive hire. Flake ice, 400 kg weekly. Transport crates, returned empty.
NOTE FROM THE CLERK: they pay six months up front and they never take fish. Bay 3 is theirs and we don't go in it. The crates go down the shore road at night, not to the ferry.
PAID. Stamped. Signed for by a driver who printed VIGOR in the name box and nothing else.

title: Cold Store Door Note
speaker: Pell
text:
Nailed inside the roller door of bay 3.
TOM - the lighthouse crank is on the nail in here, not in the hut. The keeper brought it down to lever the ice chute in March and never carried it back up, and now he's not answering his door either.
If anybody from the county asks, the crank is at the lighthouse where it belongs.
If anybody from VIGOR asks, you've never seen a crank.
- Pell

title: Note on a Wardrobe Door
speaker: Jess Arrow
text:
Pinned at child height on the inside of the wardrobe.
BABS - if you are reading this in here then you did the right thing and I am proud of you.
Count to two hundred. Slow. They go away when the water is still.
Do not open it for the noise. The noise is not me. I will knock three times and say your whole name, both names, and if I don't say both names it isn't me.
Mum.

title: Water-Stained Photograph
text:
A framed photo on a shelf of medical journals, the bottom third bloomed and buckled by damp.
A marquee, a long table, a cut ribbon. Two men shaking hands over it and holding the pose a beat too long for the camera.
On the left, younger, in a good coat: Dr. Elias Voss.
On the right, in dress uniform with the braid: Chief Warren Hale, Marrow Bay Police.
The banner behind them is legible where the water stopped: VIGOR BIOTECH - SALTMERE SITE - COMMUNITY PARTNERS.
On the back, in Calder's hand: they have known each other for eleven years. I keep forgetting that, so here it is on a wall.

title: Printed Email: Re: your resignation
speaker: Dr. Elias Voss
text:
FROM: E. Voss
TO: I. Calder
SUBJECT: Re: your resignation

Iness,

You keep using the word accident. An accident is a thing you do not repeat. I have repeated it nine times.

You met Penhallow. You shook a dying man's hand. Two months later that hand could bend rebar. You want me to call that a tragedy because the man it happened to did not stay polite.

The resignation is not accepted, because there is nothing to resign from. There is no programme. There is a sealed building under an island and a contract that says I may keep it sealed.

Come back before someone decides you are a loose end. I would rather it were me who said that to you than someone with a different job.

E.

title: Calder's Pages, 2 of 5
speaker: Dr. Ines Calder
text:
Oilcloth packet, cellar shelf, behind the preserve jars.
The hymn sheet is folded in with this page on purpose. I am not musical and I never was, so if you have found both, you are looking for the same thing I hid.
I put the bell tower key inside the organ. The verger showed me the panel behind the pipe shutter years ago, when he was proud of the thing. Play the verse and the shutter opens, the way it opens for the bell ringers.
Six notes. They are written on the sheet. Play them in the order they are written and nothing else, because that organ is loud and this town listens now.

title: Hymn Sheet: "Low Tide"
speaker: Saltmere Chapel Hymnal
text:
A single sheet, foxed at the edges, hand-ruled.
HYMN 42 - LOW TIDE - verse 1, pedal line only (as played at Saltmere)

D    G    E    D    A    D
Down  go  every  dark  anchor  down

Under the stave, in pencil: six pedals, left to right as written. The organist's hand, not Calder's.
Under that, in Calder's hand: six. Not five. Not seven. The last one is a D again and everybody gets that wrong.

title: Calder's Pages, 3 of 5
speaker: Dr. Ines Calder
text:
Same packet, cellar.
I have written the important part nine times and burned it eight. Here it is plain.
It was never a weapon. Elias wanted a treatment. He wanted to take a body that was failing and give it back more than it lost, and the strain does exactly that, which is the whole problem. It only takes in the weak, and it gives them strength they never had, and it takes everything else.
He did not build a disease. He built a success, and the success is what you met in the street.
The work is not in the city. It is below the island. Under my feet while I write this.

title: Dictaphone, Tape Side B
speaker: Dr. Ines Calder
text:
(tape hiss, a chair, water moving somewhere below)
They turned the pumps off three days ago and told the council it was a part on order. It is not a part. The basin is meant to come up. When the basin comes up, the lower doors flood and nobody goes down the stair, and the sealed building stays sealed.
(pause)
I am going to the harbor tonight to look at the gate myself. If the wheel is off the capstan then I am right and somebody took it off, and if somebody took it off then they know I have been asking.
(a long breath)
If this is the last side of this tape, the pages are in three places and I am sorry about the organ. It really is very loud.

title: Calder's Pages, 4 of 5
speaker: Dr. Ines Calder
text:
Folded into hymnal 42 in the third pew, chapel nave.
Eight months ago I signed a consent form for a man who could not hold the pen. Trial seven. We called him Subject 7 because Elias says names make people sentimental, and he is right, they do.
He killed Aldous and he killed Ruth and he did it with his hands, and the report I typed says ADVERSE EVENT, EQUIPMENT.
I typed that. Nobody made me.
So I am not writing this to be forgiven. I am writing it so that the next person who comes through this chapel does not have to work it out from scratch.

title: Calder's Pages, 5 of 5
speaker: Dr. Ines Calder
text:
Inside the vestry hymn cupboard, chapel.
Two routes, and I want this written by someone who measured it.
Breathe it as mist or drink it out of a bad tap, and it only takes if your body is already losing. The old, the sick, the worn out. Everyone else coughs and goes to work.
But a bite is a full dose straight in, and a full dose does not care how strong you are. It cares very much afterwards. The stronger the body, the worse the thing that stands up in it.
So the ones to fear here are not the grandmothers. They are the harbor men.

title: Verger's Instructions, Pinned to the Organ Bench
speaker: Howell Teague, verger
text:
FOR WHOEVER PLAYS WHILE I AM IN HOSPITAL.
The pedal board is the only thing still true on this instrument. The manuals are swollen and two stops are dead, so play the pedal line only and the congregation will cope.
The shutter over the small pipes is on the same linkage as the bell tower latch. Play the opening of 42 correctly and it draws back. Play it wrong and you get the flat chord, which is the loudest sound in this parish, and then you may start again.
Pedals are lettered on the brass. Do not improvise. I will know.

title: Hymn Board by the Chancel
text:
Slotted wooden numbers, three of the four still hanging.
THIS SUNDAY
18 - Bright Is The Morning
42 - LOW TIDE
7 - (number missing, slot empty)
EVENSONG CANCELLED - WATER
Chalked across the bottom of the board, recent, shaky: 42 only. Nothing else. Please.

title: Chapel Register, Last Page
speaker: Howell Teague, verger
text:
BURIALS, this year, entered late and badly, for which I apologise to God and the diocese.
- Aldous Frey. No body. Company sent a casket and asked us not to open it. We did not open it.
- Ruth Maddern. Same. Same casket maker.
- Ezra Penhallow. Entry struck out and rewritten: NOT DECEASED, REMOVED BY AMBULANCE, SEE CORRESPONDENCE. There is no correspondence.
- Ines Calder. Pulled out of the basin. Nobody sent a casket for her.
NOTE: the crypt lift is condemned. It goes further down than the crypt and I have never liked it.

title: Sluice Gate Operating Notice
speaker: Saltmere Harbor Board
text:
Bolted to the capstan housing, enamel, chipped.
TO CLOSE THE GATE: ship the wheel, then THREE FULL TURNS against the stop. The basin falls about a metre and a half to the mud. Allow four minutes.
TO OPEN: reverse, and stand clear of the chain.
THE WHEEL IS NOT LEFT ON THE CAPSTAN. Children. It lives chained in the bell tower with the ringing gear.
DO NOT CLOSE THE GATE WITH A VESSEL IN THE BASIN. It will sit on the bottom and you will own it.

title: Flare Locker Card
speaker: Saltmere Harbor Board
text:
Card wired to the locker handle. The locker is already forced; the hasp is bent back and the seal is torn.
CONTENTS: signal pistol, 25 mm. Cartridges, red, six. For distress use only. Replaced annually.
Six is crossed out. Three is written over it, and under that, in pencil: used three on the thing in the basin and it did not care for them. It went down and stayed down. If you are reading this, it is still in there, and it does not like burning.
No signature.

title: Chart Table: Mooring Bearings
speaker: Saltmere Harbor Board
text:
A linen chart under glass, pencil bearings taken from the lighthouse lamp room and written in the margin.
BEARINGS FROM THE LAMP (true, not magnetic)
- Chapel spire ............ 040
- Sluice gate housing ..... 115
- Drowned mooring stone ... 250
The stone is the one that only shows at low water, off the west shallows. Three boats on it in my time.
Pencilled under the list: the keeper used these three to true his mirrors every spring. He said the light was only honest if it agreed with the chart.

title: Harbor Master's Log, 3 Weeks Back
speaker: Harbor Master J. Vane
text:
0520. Recovered a female body from the basin, west wall, by the capstan housing. Identified as Dr. I. Calder, of Chapel Lane. Coat buttoned, boots laced, torch in her pocket still switched on.
Cause recorded as drowning by the county man, who did not come to the island to record it.
MY OWN NOTE, AND I WILL KEEP IT HERE: the capstan wheel was lying in the mud six feet from her and the chain was cut, not broken. Somebody took that wheel off while she was watching, or she took it off herself and somebody took it back.
I said this twice on the telephone. Nobody wrote it down.

title: Service Camera, Causeway Track
text:
A weatherproof camera on the causeway rail, battery box still warm. The card holds four clips.
CLIP 1, eight months ago, daylight: two men in Vigor coveralls welding a steel plate over the old coal hatch at the lighthouse base.
CLIP 2, same week: a flatbed with crates. The crates go to the lighthouse door. They do not come out.
CLIP 3, three weeks ago, night: a woman in a long coat walking the causeway alone toward the harbor, torch in hand. She does not come back past the camera.
CLIP 4, three days ago: one man, alone, going in with a sample case. The timestamp is the only thing on him that is legible. He does not come back past the camera either.

title: Keeper's Bearing Book
speaker: Keeper A. Rell
text:
A hardbacked book chained to the lamp room desk, open at TRUEING THE MIRRORS, SPRING.
The carriage is seized every year by salt. Ship the crank on the lower spindle and work up. ORDER IS ALWAYS LOWER, MIDDLE, UPPER. One, two, three. Never from the top, you will shear the pin.
Set each mirror on its own landmark and the beam gathers on the chart mark by the door, where the brass is worn through.
- LOWER mirror to the chapel spire .... 040
- MIDDLE mirror to the sluice ......... 115
- UPPER mirror to the ................. (the line is scratched out hard, down to the paper. A bearing was written here and somebody removed it.)
The harbor master keeps the same three on his chart table. Go and ask him, it is not a secret, it is a hill and a gate and a stone.

title: Brass Plate Under the Lens
speaker: Harlow & Sons, Opticians
text:
HARLOW & SONS - SALTMERE LIGHT - CATADIOPTRIC, 3 PANEL
Each panel runs on its own worm drive. Dials read in 5 degree steps, 000 to 355.
NO HANDLE IS SUPPLIED. The crank is the keeper's property and is to be kept in the lamp room at all times.
Scratched beside the maker's name, much later and much deeper: SERVICE DOOR BEHIND THE CHART. LATCH IS ON THE LIGHT, NOT ON A KEY. THAT WAS NOT MY IDEA.

title: Saltmere Landing
speaker: MARA
text: You're on the slipway. I watched your light come across the whole way.

title: Saltmere Landing
speaker: LEON
text: Then you've got a better view than I do. Where am I?

title: Saltmere Landing
speaker: MARA
text: Quay Row. Chapel Lane is up the hill, the market's at the top of the street, and everything between is under water.

title: Saltmere Landing
speaker: LEON
text: And you? That's your window out on the point.

title: Saltmere Landing
speaker: MARA
text: Radio station, second floor, door barricaded with a filing cabinet and a dead man's desk. I'm not coming out and you're not coming in.

title: Saltmere Landing
speaker: LEON
text: We'll see about the second half of that.

title: What's In The Water
speaker: MARA
text: Leon. Stop walking. Whatever you just saw take that body, there are more of them and they live in the deep part.

title: What's In The Water
speaker: LEON
text: They don't come up on the steps?

title: What's In The Water
speaker: MARA
text: Not if you're quiet. Walk the walls, use the doorways, and get inside a house the second you hear one break surface.

title: What's In The Water
speaker: LEON
text: Wardrobes and under beds. Like being nine again.

title: The Point
speaker: LEON
text: I'm on the point jetty. Or what's left of it, which is about four metres and a handrail.

title: The Point
speaker: MARA
text: Don't. The shallows between you and me are full of them, I can hear them on the stonework all night.

title: The Point
speaker: LEON
text: I can see your light from here.

title: The Point
speaker: MARA
text: Then look at it and go the other way. I've got water and a door. Find out what did this instead.

title: The Photograph
speaker: LEON
text: Found a photo in the dead doctor's front room. Ribbon-cutting. Voss from Vigor, shaking hands with a police chief in dress braid.

title: The Photograph
speaker: MARA
text: Which chief?

title: The Photograph
speaker: LEON
text: Hale. Marrow Bay. The man whose officers took the container off my team's hands.

title: The Photograph
speaker: MARA
text: Eleven years of each other's barbecues. That's not a coincidence, that's a friendship.

title: The Photograph
speaker: LEON
text: It's a friendship with a shipping schedule. Keep it in your head, we'll need it later.

title: Vestry Check-In
speaker: MARA
text: Relay's strong in there. Thick walls. That's the first clean signal I've had off you since the pier.

title: Vestry Check-In
speaker: LEON
text: There's a kettle and a locker and nothing trying to kill me. I'll take the ten minutes.

title: Vestry Check-In
speaker: MARA
text: Check in here whenever you pass. If you stop checking in I'll assume the worst and I'd rather not practise that.

title: Calder's Pages
speaker: LEON
text: There's a page taped under a desk in the fish market. Dr. Ines Calder, Vigor. She says she split them across three places.

title: Calder's Pages
speaker: MARA
text: Calder. The harbor master pulled her out of the basin three weeks ago. Everyone said she slipped.

title: Calder's Pages
speaker: LEON
text: She hid pages in a church, a market and her own cellar. People who slip don't do that.

title: Calder's Pages
speaker: MARA
text: So what did she find?

title: Calder's Pages
speaker: LEON
text: That none of this was meant to kill anybody. It was meant to fix people who were already dying. It worked, and this is what working looks like.

title: Calder's Pages
speaker: MARA
text: That's worse. You understand that's worse.

title: Hint: The Organ
speaker: MARA
text: That organ's the only thing in the parish that still works. If the doctor hid something, she hid it in the thing nobody would dare touch.

title: Hint: The Organ
speaker: MARA
text: Ignore the keyboards, they're swollen shut. The verger's note on the bench says pedals only, and the sheet from her cellar is the pedal line.

title: Hint: The Organ
speaker: MARA
text: Six pedals, left to right as written: D, G, E, D, A, and D again. People drop the last one. Don't.

title: The Thing In The Basin
speaker: MARA
text: Leon, that wake. Get off the low dock, get off it now.

title: The Thing In The Basin
speaker: LEON
text: I've seen it. It's about eleven metres of eel and it's wearing someone's net.

title: The Thing In The Basin
speaker: MARA
text: You can't fight that in water, nobody can. Take the water away from it.

title: The Thing In The Basin
speaker: LEON
text: The gate. Three turns and a metre and a half of mud. Keep talking, I'll be busy.

title: Hint: The Sluice Gate
speaker: MARA
text: Shooting it in deep water is just noise. The basin is the only thing on your side down there, so change it.

title: Hint: The Sluice Gate
speaker: MARA
text: The capstan is on the west wall with the notice bolted to it. Ship the wheel from the bell tower and it's three full turns against the stop.

title: Hint: The Sluice Gate
speaker: MARA
text: One turn per pass, that's all you get. When it beaches, the sac behind the jaw comes open. Put a flare in it.

title: Hint: The Lighthouse Lens
speaker: MARA
text: There's no keyhole on that service door, is there. So the lock isn't a lock, it's the light.

title: Hint: The Lighthouse Lens
speaker: MARA
text: The keeper's book sets each mirror on a landmark, lower then middle then upper. His third bearing's scratched out, but the harbor master's chart has all three.

title: Hint: The Lighthouse Lens
speaker: MARA
text: Lower to the spire, 040. Middle to the sluice, 115. Upper to the drowned mooring stone, 250. In that order or you'll shear the pin.

title: Below The Island
speaker: LEON
text: The latch dropped. There's a door behind the keeper's chart and a stone stair going down.

title: Below The Island
speaker: MARA
text: Down to what? There's nothing under that rock but rock.

title: Below The Island
speaker: LEON
text: Painted steel, cable trays, and air moving up at me. Calder's last page says the work is below the island. She meant it literally.

title: Below The Island
speaker: MARA
text: Then I'll lose you on the radio the moment you're under the water line.

title: Below The Island
speaker: LEON
text: Keep the set warm and the light on. I'll come up somewhere.
